decisions.essenceRationale: Working a list (capture, reword, discard, complete/reopen, toggle all, clear completed) is the one thing every team member and every agent acting for them comes to this product to do. It is the fixed reference behavior the mission commits to and will not grow. It stays the same whether the caller is a person in the web app, a person in a host workspace, or agent tooling, and whatever store keeps the list. The product's differentiator is not the verbs themselves. It is that one kept, team-side list behaves identically to every party and every surface, with each change landing once and showing everywhere. That abstraction, a new name not in the founder's list, subsumes six raw requests and the agent-tooling request.

decisions.essenceRationale: Every party that comes back to a list first needs that same list recalled exactly as it was left: the same wording, order and done states, whatever tab, device, host or agent they come from. They then look at it through a view, with a true count of what remains. The guarantee that the list is kept and recalled on the team's side and seen identically everywhere is why the founder wants a real service rather than a browser toy. It does not change over time and is shared by every member and agent. It subsumes three raw requests (switch views, see items left, find my list next time) and the embedded-host request under one abstraction that reads but never changes the list.

listAccess.title: ListAccess — atomic kept-list verbs over one member's durable todo list (ResourceAccess, Postgres binding). Callers: ListManager only, sync. Every op is scoped to exactly one member; nothing reaches across members. No events, no queued ops, no Temporal. Durability: an acknowledged change is committed before the op returns; reads see every acknowledged change (read-your-writes). Bulk ops (SettleAll, SweepCompleted) are applied in one store transaction, never half-applied. Store technology and its binding (connection, credentials from hosting configuration/secrets) are hidden behind this contract.

ListFault.description: Error model. Every op returns a Go error whose kind is one of these values; store-specific errors never leak. todoNotFound (terminal): ReviseWording/SettleCompletion named a todoId absent from the member's list — ListManager decides how to reconcile (e.g. another surface removed it). todoIdConflict (terminal): AppendTodo retried a todoId already kept with different wording. invalidRequest (terminal): empty memberId or todoId. storeUnavailable (transient, retry-safe): the store could not be reached or the transaction aborted; nothing was applied. Idempotency: AppendTodo is idempotent on todoId (same id + same wording returns the kept todo); ReviseWording, SettleCompletion, SettleAll, SweepCompleted are idempotent by nature; WithdrawTodo of an absent todo succeeds. Orchestration guidance (non-normative): 5s per-call timeout, retry storeUnavailable only.

Member.description: The team member whose list is worked, as resolved by IdentityAccess.recognizeActingParty and passed through by ListManager. memberId is an opaque, stable identifier; ListAccess keys every list on it and never interprets it. An empty memberId is rejected (ListFault invalidRequest, terminal).

memberId.description: Opaque stable member identifier from IdentityAccess.

Todo.description: One kept todo: its id, wording and done flag. The shape is fixed (no dates, priority, tags, ordering, sharing). Lists are returned in capture order (the order AppendTodo first accepted each todoId).

done.description: true when the todo is done (completed), false when active.

todoId.description: Caller-minted id (ListManager mints it, e.g. a UUID, before the first AppendTodo attempt so retries are recognisable). Unique within a member's list.

wording.description: The todo's wording, stored verbatim. ListAccess applies no blank-wording or trimming rule; that is ListManager's.
